decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed development, having regard to its layout, domestic facilities, scale, physical and functional separation from the host dwelling and independent access from Patricesy Mews, would amount to a self-contained residential unit rather than an ancillary outbuilding. The creation of the self-contained residential unit on private residential garden land would result in an inappropriate form of backland development which fails to maintain the local character of the site. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy LP7 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Reason : 2 - The proposed development, by reason of its siting, scale, height, massing, form and appearance, would result in a visually prominent form of development, and erode the established pattern of development and openness and verdant character of the rear garden setting. Consequently, the proposal would fail to preserve the character and appearance of the Westbridge Road Conservation Area and cause harm to the setting of the locally listed building at No.30 Westbridge Road. The public benefits of the proposal would not outweigh the heritage harm. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies LP1, LP3 and LP7 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), Policies D4 and HC1 of the London Plan (2021), Policies HE6, HE7 and HE9 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), and sections 72(1) of the Planning (listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990.

Reason : 3 - The proposed dwelling would provide a poor standard of accommodation for future occupiers by reason of the basement lightwells and openings screened by hit and miss brickwork, resulting in an oppressive internal living environment and an unacceptable standard of outlook. Furthermore, discrepancies between the submitted Daylight and Sunlight Assessment and submitted drawings mean that it has not been satisfactorily demonstrated that adequate levels of daylight and sunlight would be achieved within the proposed dwelling. The proposal would therefore fail to provide high-quality living environment for future occupiers, contrary to Policy LP27 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023) and Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021).

Reason : 4 - In the absence of adequate arboricultural and ecological information, insufficient information has been submitted to demonstrate the effects of the proposed development on existing trees within and adjoining the site and protected species, including bats. It has therefore not been demonstrated that existing trees could be retained and protected or that the proposed development would avoid unacceptable harm to protected species. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies LP3, LP55 and LP56 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021), the Wandsworth Biodiversity SPD (2025) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Reason : 5 - Insufficient information has been submitted to demonstrate that suitable and convenient arrangements could be made for the collection of refuse and recycling, or that adequate access would be available for fire appliances and other emergency vehicles. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy LP2 and L13 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), Policies D5 and D12 of the London Plan (2021), Wandsworth Reuse, Recycling and Waste SPD (2025) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Reason : 6 - The proposed development would result in the creation of a self-contained residential unit within Flood Zone 3a. The proposal is not supported by a Sequential Test or Exception Test as required by the National Standing Advice. The development has therefore not been demonstrated to be acceptable in principle in this location having regard to flood risk, contrary to Policy LP12 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), Policies SI12 of the London Plan and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Reason : 7 - Insufficient information has been submitted to demonstrate that suitable and convenient arrangements could be made for the collection of refuse and recycling, or that adequate access would be available for fire appliances and other emergency vehicles. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy LP2 and L13 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), Policies D5 and D12 of the London Plan (2021), Wandsworth Reuse, Recycling and Waste SPD (2025) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Reason : 8 - In dealing with this application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to make available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies in the Local Plan as well as offering a full pre application advice service. However, we have been unable to seek solutions to problems as the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.
description: Demolition of existing single storey (plus basement) garage/outbuilding and erection of new two-storey (plus basement) outbuilding with solar panels to rear garden.
